chapter: Jaco, honors, teaching and looking ahead
title: The NEA Jazz Master award, 2009
summary: He recalls fellow honorees and Gerald Wilson speaking for Snooky Young.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Well, what about the NEA Jazz Master Fellowship? What, when you received that three years ago…
Yeah, that was… that was the same thing. In those… that, that year was Jimmy Cobb. Lee Konitz. The engineer from [inaudible] Van Gelder.
Rudy Van Gelder from Jersey. I mean, there were six, six… nobility.
Nobility… noble… Is that… yeah, there was, was an important…
So then, you know you’re not only in Belgian royalty but you’re in jazz royalty, too.
Yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Well, I can’t read well.
Yeah, yeah. So… let me see. No, here… No, the year is actually 2009, so this is wrong. George Benson, Jimmy Cobb…
Lee Konitz, Rudy Van Gelder, Snooky Young. Snooky. [laughs]
Yeah. Yeah, so 2009 was the year.
But I think Snooky was not somebody… two other guys came. Frank West and the California band leader.
Gerald Wilson talked about the achievements of Snooky, who was sitting, you know. I remember that.
